title: The preflight batchMint call-site sweep missed two scripts that still bind the legacy scalar-minReward signature — correct today, silently break on the story-072 cutover, and absent from the story's feedback list
propagation: PROPAGATES-TO-MAINNET (break-on-cutover only — a tooling break at the moment of the story-072 cutover, not a mainnet state impact)
specText: Story 073 Preflight line 491 (ticked): 'grep -rn "batchMint(" script/ scripts/ test/ and list every call site needing the 4-arg / length-3 form (expect TestNudgePayout.s.sol, TestBalancerDonation.s.sol).' Story 073 Change 2 line 505 (ticked): 'Update every batchMint( call site found in preflight to the 4-arg / length-3 minRewards form, re-fetching getNudgeTokens() rather than hardcoding 3.'
faithfulnessRouting: F-03 — PRIMARY. Routed to the spec-conformance report at honest severity. QA severity, but NOT bundled into QA/gas noise: Law 2 requires a story deviation to remain visible to the owner, and the story-072 feedback omission is the actionable part.
description: Story 073 preflight line 491 instructs `grep -rn "batchMint(" script/ scripts/ test/` and to list EVERY call site needing the new form, parenthetically expecting TestNudgePayout.s.sol and TestBalancerDonation.s.sol. Two further call sites exist inside that grep's own scope and were not listed: script/PreviewBatchMint40.s.sol declares the legacy signature at :55 (`function batchMint(uint256 count, address recipient, uint256 paymentAmount, uint256 minReward)`) and calls it at :145, and script/interactions/SimulateMainnetNudgeMint.s.sol calls `batch.batchMint(count, recipient, payment, 0)` at :77. Both bind the legacy SCALAR minReward; BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:470 takes `uint256[] calldata minRewards`. (Note: both forms are four-argument; the difference is the fourth parameter's type, not the arity.)
impact: Correct at this commit — both scripts target the live mainnet legacy BatchNFTMinter and match its signature — but both break the moment story 072 cuts the mainnet index-4 minter over to BatchNFTMinterMultiToken, and story 073's 'findings to feed back into story 072' set omits them, so nothing carries the problem across the cutover boundary. Aggravating detail: SimulateMainnetNudgeMint.s.sol:77 wraps the call in try/catch and its low-level branch merely logs 'REVERT low-level', so post-cutover it will not fail loudly but will emit output resembling a simulation result — in a tool whose purpose is to tell an operator whether a mainnet mint will succeed.
attackPath: No attack path. Completeness gap in an instructed sweep.
Line 491 instructs `grep -rn "batchMint(" script/ scripts/ test/` and to list EVERY call site, parenthetically expecting two. Two others exist within that exact grep scope and were not listed.
script/PreviewBatchMint40.s.sol:55 declares `function batchMint(uint256 count, address recipient, uint256 paymentAmount, uint256 minReward)` — the legacy SCALAR-minReward form — and calls it at :145.
script/interactions/SimulateMainnetNudgeMint.s.sol:77 calls `batch.batchMint(count, recipient, payment, 0)`, again binding the scalar form.
BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:470 takes `uint256[] calldata minRewards`. On the story-072 cutover these bindings no longer resolve against the deployed contract.
evidence: grep -rn 'batchMint(' script/ at 3fb4e34 returns, besides the two scripts the story lists: script/PreviewBatchMint40.s.sol:13 (comment), :55 (interface declaration, scalar minReward), :101 (comment), :145 (call `minter.batchMint(MINT_COUNT, deployer, payment, minReward)`); and script/interactions/SimulateMainnetNudgeMint.s.sol:77 (`try batch.batchMint(count, recipient, payment, 0)`). Target signatures: lib/nft-staking/src/BatchNFTMinter.sol:238 (legacy) vs lib/nft-staking/src/BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:470 `function batchMint(uint256 count, address recipient, uint256 paymentAmount, uint256[] calldata minRewards)`. Story line 491 verified ticked and its grep scope verified to include both files.
recommendation: Add script/PreviewBatchMint40.s.sol (:55 interface, :145 call) and script/interactions/SimulateMainnetNudgeMint.s.sol (:77) to story 073's 'findings to feed back into story 072' list, and convert both to the `uint256[] calldata minRewards` form as part of the cutover — re-fetching getNudgeTokens() rather than hardcoding a length, exactly as line 505 requires of the other two. Independently, replace SimulateMainnetNudgeMint's low-level catch branch with a hard failure or a clearly-labelled 'SIGNATURE MISMATCH' diagnostic, so a post-cutover ABI break cannot read as a simulation result.

severityRationale: QA, matching the auditor's proposal. Deliberately NOT raised to Low, and the reasoning is worth stating because a break-on-cutover flag invites inflation. WHY NOT LOW. (1) NO IMPACT NOW OR LATER, IN ANY SEVERITY-BEARING SENSE. Both scripts are correct at this commit and both are read-only preview/simulation tools — PreviewBatchMint40 is a named preview and SimulateMainnetNudgeMint is a fork simulation; neither broadcasts. After the cutover the worst outcome is a failed preview, i.e. a developer-facing inconvenience, not a protocol effect. C4 Low still wants state handling, a spec deviation with consequence, or an operational risk; a stale binding in a read-only tool is the thinnest of these. (2) THE BREAK IS LOUD IN THE PRINCIPAL CASE. PreviewBatchMint40 binds the wrong signature through a local interface and will simply revert on an unmatched selector. (3) Rule 4 — when uncertain, classify lower — and overstatement is a documented rejection cause. WHY NOT DROPPED, and what the fix is actually for. (1) IT IS A GENUINE LAW-2 DEVIATION. Line 491 does not ask for a survey, it instructs an exhaustive grep over `script/ scripts/ test/` and to list EVERY call site. Both missed scripts sit squarely inside that grep's own stated scope, so the sweep was not merely incomplete by bad luck — it under-delivered against its literal instruction, and line 505's 'update every batchMint( call site found in preflight' inherits the shortfall. (2) THE OMISSION FROM THE FEEDBACK LIST IS THE DURABLE PART. Story 073 explicitly maintains a 'findings to feed back into story 072' set, and these two call sites are not in it — so the one mechanism that would carry the problem across the cutover boundary does not have it. (3) ONE AGGRAVATOR WORTH RECORDING, which is why the fix is owed rather than optional: SimulateMainnetNudgeMint.s.sol:77 wraps its call in try/catch with `catch (bytes memory low) { console.log("REVERT low-level"); }`, so post-cutover it will not fail loudly — it will print a low-level revert that reads like a simulation result. That is quiet, and quiet failures in a tool whose whole purpose is to tell an operator whether a mainnet mint will succeed are how a wrong conclusion gets drawn. QA severity with a mandatory fix, not QA severity as a shrug. PROPAGATES-TO-MAINNET is retained as a BREAK-ON-CUTOVER flag, not as an impact claim: nothing propagates to mainnet state; what propagates is a tooling break that arrives exactly when the operator is relying on those tools. LAW-2 ROUTING: despite QA severity, tagged faithfulness:true and routed to the spec-conformance report as F-03 so it reaches the owner and the story-072 feedback list. It must NOT disappear into a QA/gas bundle — that is precisely the burial Law 2 forbids. TERMINOLOGY CORRECTION carried from the auditor's draft: the legacy form is not '3-arg'. Both forms take four arguments; the legacy binds a SCALAR `uint256 minReward` and the multi-token form binds `uint256[] calldata minRewards` (BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:470). The corrected description is used throughout so the fix instruction is unambiguous.
classifierNotes: Description corrected from the auditor's '3-arg batchMint' to the verified 'legacy scalar-minReward 4-arg form' — both signatures take four parameters and differ in the fourth's type (uint256 vs uint256[]). Getting this right matters because the fix instruction is a signature change. Kept SEPARATE from FAITH-001: FAITH-001 is a script that survived BECAUSE it has no batchMint call site at all and was nonetheless credited with coverage; FAITH-003 is two scripts that DO have call sites and were missed by the sweep. Different defects, different fixes. ACTION with an owner-visible deadline: add both call sites to story 073's 'findings to feed back into story 072' list BEFORE the cutover broadcast, since after it they are silently wrong.

parkedItemsCarriedForward.title: ERC4626YieldStrategy.previewRedeem / previewDeposit view passthroughs still STATICCALL the underlying vault — the story-060 / YS-01 Tokemak fix is one-directional
parkedItemsCarriedForward.sourceVerification: Read against the TOP-LEVEL submodule HEAD lib/reflax-yield-vault (not a nested stale pin). :73-75 `return vault.previewDeposit(assets);` and :83-85 `return vault.previewRedeem(shares);`, both declared `external view` => Solidity emits STATICCALL. Twenty lines below, :110-115 credits principal via `vault.convertToAssets(sharesReceived)` with an in-source comment naming the exact hazard: 'Use convertToAssets (NOT previewRedeem): convertToAssets is ERC4626-mandated STATICCALL-safe, whereas some real vaults (e.g. Tokemak Autopools) mutate state inside previewRedeem and revert with StateChangeDuringStaticCall when called as an external view.' The authors therefore knew the hazard and hardened ONE call site.
parkedItemsCarriedForward.whyItMatters: Against a real Tokemak Autopool these two views revert for every caller, always; against MockAutoDOLA (plain un-overridden OZ ERC4626) they return a clean number, always. The local rig therefore reports green on the exact behaviour that already bricked this project's YS-swap suite. Blast radius today is UI/keeper reads (no first-party on-chain caller found), which is why this is parked for triage rather than asserted as a Medium.

secondaryGapsInTheSameMockSection: No maxRedeem/maxWithdraw check before `vault.redeem` in _disposeShares (:128-135): against a real Autopool with a liquid reserve below the request, user withdrawals brick. Locally impossible to reproduce.

MockAutoDOLA._updateYield() mints assets into the vault BEFORE super._deposit mints shares, so convertToAssets(sharesReceived) > amount and creditedPrincipal at :115 can EXCEED the deposited amount — the precise opposite of that line's stated intent. Any local invariant asserting 'principal is never over-credited' passes VACUOUSLY. Flagged because a vacuous-harness result is a known repeat failure mode in this repo.
